primary_sources.role: equation 17 conductivity finite difference, Geff/hp infiltration gradient, equation 18 difference from 2008 equation 6, Green-Ampt and infinite-depth limits

source_bound_reasoning: Talbot-Ogden 2008 equation 6 has the Green-Ampt-form capillary term plus K(theta_d), divided by theta_d-theta_i.
Ogden et al. 2015 state equation 18 is identical to 2008 equation 6 except for subtraction of K(theta_i) from K(theta_d).
Ogden et al. 2015 replace the infiltration hydraulic-gradient capillary length by positive G_eff plus surface ponding h_p.
Ogden et al. 2015 state the infinite-depth limit is the finite-difference approximation of dK/dtheta.
Ogden et al. 2015 state the one-bin deep well-drained limit is Green-Ampt with G_eff=H_c, theta_d=theta_e, K(theta_i)=0 and z=F/DeltaTheta.
executable_checks: one-bin Green-Ampt infiltration-rate identity for positive H_c and optional h_p
zero capillary and zero ponding reduces exactly to the conductivity finite-difference velocity
K(theta_d)=K(theta_i) leaves only the capillary/ponding contribution
dimensions are L/T for every tested finite input
nonpositive theta_d-theta_i or nonpositive z_j fails closed
hard_nonclaims: No rainfall/snowmelt allocation or ponding lifecycle qualification.
No capillary-drive G_eff closure implementation qualification.
No front merge, falling-slug conversion or groundwater interaction qualification.
hard_guards: Do not infer dry-bin initialization from this ODE gate.
Do not replace G_eff with an arbitrary suction parameter in later production code without a separate closure contract.
Do not change sign conventions silently.
Mass conservation remains a separate finite-volume ownership requirement even if the ODE algebra passes.
